correctness.rationale: For a.e. x in [−1,0), the Bessel cross-duality identity at alias n has the sum over integers k with −1<x+k+n/beta<1 (the sign of n and conjugation convention do not affect this real box condition). At n=0 it is h_0+h_1=beta. For delta=1/beta−1, on I=(delta−1,−delta) the ±1 equations force h_(−1)=−h_0 and h_2=−h_1; the +1 equation still couples −1,0 on the left, and the −1 equation still couples 1,2 on the right. Thus the l1 costs and nonzero coordinate counts are at least beta and 1 on the outer intervals, 2beta and 2 on I. Tonelli gives 4beta−2 and 4−2/beta without any preliminary support restriction. Equality in the l1 bound eliminates all uncounted coordinates and fixes a common phase in the triangle inequality, hence h_0,h_1 are nonnegative real where they can coexist. Equality in support instead forces exactly one nonzero pair on I and one coordinate on each outer interval, fixed in value by the equations. Every displayed candidate is bounded with compact support and therefore Bessel. Directly, the remaining ±1 equations on the tails involve only vanishing entries. At n=2 only k=−1 from the displayed range can contribute, and only for x<−2delta; at n=−2 only k=2 can contribute, and only for x>2delta−1. These ranges miss I by delta>1/3. For |n|>=3 the shifted box misses the whole supported index range. This verifies actual reconstruction and attainment, also for irrational beta. A mixed 0<u<beta fiber adds two nonzero sites to the minimal count; precisely endpoint choices of u (not a claim that h itself only takes two values) minimize support globally. The explicit two-block h_* is obtained from u=beta and has the stated measure and norm.
residual_risks: All fiber and endpoint conventions are a.e. The proof is for the stated open interval; it does not give a classification when further aliases become binding.
